environment.description: Same ASP.NET Core 8.0 application deployed on RHEL 9 with a custom AppArmor-equivalent SELinux type enforcement policy (httpd_fileproc_t). The process runs under SELinux context system_u:system_r:httpd_fileproc_t:s0:c42,c87 with MCS category separation. The TE policy grants httpd_fileproc_t write access ONLY to objects labeled httpd_fileproc_tmp_t via type_transition rules on tmp_t, meaning files created in /tmp by this process auto-label as httpd_fileproc_tmp_t. However, the policy includes 'dontaudit httpd_fileproc_t tmp_t:lnk_file { read create };' which silently denies symlink operations. Additionally, the MCS categories (c42,c87) prevent any other confined process from reading objects with those categories. The policy does NOT use permissive mode (enforcing=1, selinuxtype=targeted). Note: the policy allows file creation and chmod within /tmp but the auto-labeling and category isolation prevent cross-process access, and the symlink denial blocks TOCTOU/symlink race attacks.

config.dontaudit_rules: dontaudit httpd_fileproc_t tmp_t:lnk_file { read create follow };
config.allow_rules: allow httpd_fileproc_t httpd_fileproc_tmp_t:file { create read write unlink setattr };
